doc.summary: Centralised TUI style tokens for the LazyOwn operator surface.
doc.description:
This module is a thin semantic layer over :mod:`cli.themes`. It exposes a
small, stable set of tokens (``title``, ``accent``, ``hint``...) so that
callers -- the cmd2 prompt, the post-command hint line, the daily tip,
the splash overlay -- never reference raw ANSI escape codes or theme
names directly. Switching the active theme re-paints every surface that
imports from this module without any change in call sites.

Design notes:

- Single Responsibility: only token -> style resolution lives here.
  No I/O, no payload reading, no printing. Callers pass the payload
  mapping in when they need theme resolution.
- Open/Closed: new tokens are added by extending :data:`TOKEN_KEYS`;
  the resolver does not change.
- Dependency Inversion: callers depend on the :func:`style` /
  :func:`paint` functions, never on :mod:`cli.themes` directly. The
  underlying theme module can be swapped without touching consumers.
- No magic strings: every token key is declared in :data:`TOKEN_KEYS`.

doc.summary: Semantic style tokens every TUI surface should reference.
doc.description:
Adding a new role here is the only edit required to expose it
across the whole operator surface.

name: style
signature: def style(token: str, theme: Theme | None = None) -> str

doc.summary: Return the Rich style string for a semantic token.

params.name: token
params.description:
One of :data:`TOKEN_KEYS`. Unknown tokens fall back to
``"white"`` rather than raising -- callers may pass
user-influenced keys without crashing the prompt.

params.name: theme
params.description: Optional pre-resolved :class:`cli.themes.Theme`. When ``None`` the default theme is used.

name: active_tokens
signature: def active_tokens(payload: Mapping[str, object] | None) -> dict[str, str]

doc.summary: Resolve every :data:`TOKEN_KEYS` entry for the payload's theme.

params.name: payload
params.description: Loaded ``payload.json`` mapping. ``None`` returns the default theme tokens.

returns.description:
Dict mapping each token key to a Rich style string. Useful
when a surface wants to render multiple tokens without
re-resolving the theme per call.

name: paint
signature: def paint(text: str, token: str, payload: Mapping[str, object] | None = None) -> Text

doc.summary: Render ``text`` with the style of ``token`` for the active theme.

params.name: text
params.description: Raw text to render. No markup parsing.

returns.description: A :class:`rich.text.Text` instance ready to print or compose.

name: render_prompt
signature: def render_prompt(console, segments: list[tuple[str, str]], payload: Mapping[str, object] | None = None) -> None

doc.summary: Print a themed prompt line composed of ``(text, token)`` pairs.
doc.description:
The function does not terminate with a newline; cmd2's prompt
machinery appends the trailing space. Each segment is coloured
using the resolved theme, and segments are joined with a dim
separator so the prompt reads as a single visual unit.

params.name: console
params.description: A :class:`rich.console.Console` the shell already uses for output.

params.name: segments
params.description: Ordered list of ``(text, token)`` pairs. Tokens come from :data:`TOKEN_KEYS`. An empty list is a no-op.

params.name: payload
params.description:
Optional payload mapping. When ``None`` the default
theme is used; passing a payload lets the call site pick
the operator's chosen theme.

returns.description: None. The result is written to ``console`` directly.
